2	//! coding worker. The flags map one-to-one onto [`crate::work::Options`]; the guards

4	
5	use clap::Args;
6	
7	use crate::work::Options;
8	
9	/// Arguments of `c3 work`. `--task` is required by every form; `--brief`/`--provider`
10	/// by a run (`--status`/`--wait` read the records only, `--detach-id` is internal).
11	#[derive(Args, Debug)]
12	pub struct WorkArgs {
13	    /// The task slug (letters, digits, dot, dash, underscore): the collab dir's task.
14	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
15	    pub task: String,
16	    /// The brief file (repo-relative or absolute); c3 never writes briefs.
17	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
18	    pub brief: String,
19	    /// The roster label of the worker (engine claude, role "worker").
20	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
21	    pub provider: String,
22	    /// The model id ("" = the roster entry's model, same endpoint).
23	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
24	    pub model: String,
25	    /// Extra ask text appended to the prompt after the brief.
26	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
27	    pub prompt: String,
28	    /// low | medium | high | xhigh ("" = send none).
29	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
30	    pub effort: String,
31	    /// The turn cap (0 = 80).
32	    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 0)]
33	    pub max_turns: i64,
34	    /// The run timeout in seconds (0 = 3600).
35	    #[arg(long, default_value_t = 0)]
36	    pub timeout_sec: i64,
37	    /// A Claude Code --allowedTools pattern (repeatable; "" list = the cargo defaults).
38	    /// A pattern naming git is refused: a worker never commits.
39	    #[arg(long = "allow", value_name = "PATTERN")]
40	    pub allow: Vec<String>,
41	    /// Where work runs are stored; a relative path resolves against the repo root.
42	    #[arg(long, default_value = ".collab")]
43	    pub collab_dir: String,
44	    /// Start the run in the background and print the come-back commands.
45	    #[arg(long)]
46	    pub detach: bool,
47	    /// Print the work runs of the task (exit 0 done, 1 died/timed out, 2 running).
48	    #[arg(long)]
49	    pub status: bool,
50	    /// Wait until the task's work runs are done, then print as --status.
51	    #[arg(long)]
52	    pub wait: bool,
53	    /// The work run id (or its beginning) --status/--wait narrows to.
54	    #[arg(long, default_value = "")]
55	    pub id: String,
56	    /// --wait's timeout in seconds (0 = the run's own budget).
57	    #[arg(long)]
58	    pub wait_timeout_sec: Option<i64>,
59	    /// INTERNAL: the background process of --detach; never pass it yourself.
60	    #[arg(long, default_value = "", hide = true)]
61	    pub detach_id: String,
62	}
63

65	    crate::work::run(Options {
66	        task: args.task,
67	        brief: args.brief,
68	        provider: args.provider,
69	        model: args.model,
70	        prompt: args.prompt,
71	        effort: args.effort,

9	# Coordinate (c3)
10	
11	The C3 port supports one coordinator host: **Claude Code**. This skill is the coordination
12	layer over the `c3` binary. (The multi-host coordination story — Codex CLI, Z Code, Kimi Code,
13	a plain shell — stays with the `codex-consult` PowerShell bridge and is deliberately not ported
14	here.) The consultation procedure itself is the `consult` skill; wiring reviewers is
15	`setup-providers`.
16	
17	## Invariants
18	
19	- **You are the coordinator and the judge by default.** Workers execute, reviewers advise, you
20	  decide and verify. Never redo a worker's work once it reports — read the report and verify in
21	  your own loop; what still needs checking is a new, scoped task.
22	- **One objective per worker.** Brief it precisely the first time: the objective, the exact
23	  files, the numbers its result is measured against, what it must not touch, the report shape. A
24	  launch, a wait and a re-brief cost more than a brief written once.
25	- **English to reviewers and workers.** Briefs, prompts and handoff titles are in English;
26	  source material in another language is translated or summarised, never pasted.
27	- **Wait without blocking; keep the prompt cache warm.** Poll a state file or `c3 consult --task
28	  <task> --status`; never sit in a blocking foreground wait longer than the shell tool's limit.
29	  After the cache's lifetime the next request re-writes the whole context, so a large context
30	  must not go cold by oversight.
31	  - *Running work* (keeps the wake armed, idle count zero): a worker or subagent that has not
32	    reported; a detached consultation or panel (start `c3 consult --task <task> --wait` in the
33	    background - its exit is the signal - or poll `--status`); a long shell job (a suite, a
34	    build); a window you gave another session, until it says it is done; an operator step with a
35	    named end ("I install it and come back"); a cooldown with a named end (a provider's
36	    `retry_after`, a quota window). Idle is only: none of these, and nothing can be done without
37	    the operator.
38	  - *The means in Claude Code:* a Monitor or a background wait is the primary signal; the
39	    `ScheduleWakeup` tool is the heartbeat - about 20 minutes (1200 s), armed at the first
40	    delegation or wait of the session and kept while running work goes on. Every wake: small
41	    reads only (a state file's tail, `c3 consult --task <task> --status`); one line when nothing
42	    finished. Anything finished or needing action is activity: act, and the idle count restarts.
43	  - *Idle:* idle wake 1 - one line in the state file ("idle since <time>"); idle wake 2 - write
44	    the handover on disk, stop the wakeups, and tell the operator in one line the cheap ways
45	    back: a fresh session from the state file; `/compact` is the operator's to run.
46	  - *Compaction* only at a wave boundary (the report is read, the state is on disk) and only
47	    while the cache is warm. In Claude Code the agent has no means to compact itself: while work
48	    runs, keep the context warm however long the wait; when idle, hand over as above.
49	- **Rate every consultation** once its reply is read (`c3 findings --task <task> --rate <n>
50	  --useful yes|partly|no`). A routed panel draws its seats from these marks.
51	- **Ask the operator before going on without a required reviewer** — when one the topic needs is
52	  out, or `--require` refuses the run, tell the operator who is out and until when.
53	
54	## The live-member rule
55	
56	While an `agy` or `muse` member runs (a single run or a panel member, detached or not), write
57	NOTHING under the collab directory or the working tree — `state.md`, notes and findings stores
58	included — and run no git command. Both engines are checked by evidence: a change during an
59	`agy` run FAILS that member; during a `muse` run it WARNS; either way the reviewer read a moving
60	target. This binds your workers too: hold a writing worker until `--status` says the run is
61	done, then write what you queued. (The `http` engine never touches the machine — it only warns.)
62	
63	## The coordinator record
64	
65	- The coordinator's session identity never reaches a reviewer child. `c3` scrubs the host
66	  markers (`CODEX_SESSION_ID`, the `CLAUDE_CODE_*` session ids, the messaging socket and token,
67	  `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, every `CODEX_SANDBOX*`, and the `ZCODE_*` / `ZCODE_PLUGIN*`)
68	  from every reviewer CLI and launcher probe. The ledger records the removed NAMES in
69	  `child_env_scrubbed`, never a value. The operator's own settings, the plugin roots and the
70	  provider keys are kept.
71	- The coordinator's identity is recorded once per run in the ledger `coordinator`
72	  `{provider, model, engine, host, source}`. `host` is `claude-code` when the Claude Code
73	  markers are present, else `unknown`. Set `CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR` to `<provider> :: <model>`
74	  (optionally ` [<engine>]`), a roster position `#<n>` or a provider label to name the
75	  coordinator's own model; a reviewer the bridge seats that IS your model gets a warning (never a
76	  refusal), and an unparseable value is refused before anything starts. Keep the operator's value
77	  when it is set — do not guess your own.
78	
79	## The bridge's own background means
80	
81	Prefer these to the host's own backgrounding. Full mechanics and exit codes: the `consult`
82	skill's `reference.md`.
83	
84	- `c3 consult --detach ...` — run a consultation or a panel in the background, return at once
85	  with the detach id, its status file and the come-back commands. Checked first: a refusal comes
86	  back immediately, nothing written.
87	- `c3 consult --task <task> --status [--id <id>]` — read status only, never blocks (0 done+usable,
88	  1 done with a failure or died, 2 running). `--status --prune` removes files of runs done/died
89	  > 7 days.
90	- `c3 consult --task <task> --wait [--id <id>] [--wait-timeout-sec <s>]` — block until done; keep
91	  `<s>` below your tool's command timeout.
92	- `c3 consult --task <task> --kick --member <NN> [--id <id>]` — stop ONE hung member; its partial
93	  is salvaged and the panel goes on. Ask the operator before kicking a merely-slow member.
94	
95	Park a detached run in the task's `state.md` (the detach id, the brief path, the come-back
96	command); a later session finds it there and in the SessionStart line.
97	
98	**Quota windows (wave 8).** Before a wave of reviews on a subscription plan, read the QUOTA column of
99	`c3 providers` (`5h 96% until 18:32; wk 15% until Oct 20`): a quota window at 98 % or more makes
100	the reviewer out until its reset, like a usage limit - ask the operator whether to wait or to go on
101	without that reviewer. Keep review threads small: prefer `--mode new` with a brief that names the
102	earlier reply over forking a large thread (a parent rollout over `CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB` is refused,
103	it would be replayed on every tool call); the bridge stops a run at `--budget` (90 % by default) with its
104	partial kept, and turns the reviewer's sub-agents off.
105	
106	## Supporting c3 commands
107	
108	- `c3 pack --brief <b> --out <o> [--focus <glob>] [--budget <n>] [--task <t>]` — build a
109	  sanitizing reviewer pack (with a `.pack.json` sidecar) for the `http` engine or for a chat
110	  model; the index feeds the periphery when present, else a lexical neighbourhood.
111	- `c3 explain --claim "<c>" [--focus <glob>] [--audience <who>] --yes` — an explainer pack for
112	  one claim. **It leaves the machine only after you confirm** (`--yes` skips the prompt).
113	- `c3 snapshot [--delta] [--depth 0-9] [--budget <n>] [--focus <glob>]` — a repository snapshot,
114	  optionally a git delta since the last full snapshot's anchor.
115	- `c3 index build|rebuild|query|stats` — the local code index (embedded SurrealDB, per project; opt-in: `cargo install --features index-surreal`, else it reports `none`).
116	  Never required for a consultation; `query` is BM25 + reciprocal-rank with a bounded 1-hop
117	  expansion.
118	- `c3 router simulate|replay|priors|explain` — routing insight: `explain` prints the score table
119	  the next panel draw would use, one line per roster lineage; `replay` confirms a routed panel's
120	  seats from the ledger.
121	- `c3 telemetry status` (the on/off status and instance id), `c3 complain "<text>"` and
122	  `c3 forget-me` (the maintainer intake; both confirm before sending). Telemetry is on by
123	  default, carries outcome classes only — never task names, prompts, briefs, paths or keys — and
124	  `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off` switches it off.
125	
126	## Worker-tier contract
127	
128	Pick the tier by what the task needs; the names stay, the models behind them change.
129	
130	- **Deep reasoning that needs judgment** (`opus-worker`) — novel code, multi-file debugging,
131	  build-and-fix loops. Writes.
132	- **Well-specified, pattern-following execution** (`sonnet-worker`, the default) — a known change
133	  across files, tests to a pattern, doc updates, running a suite and reporting. Writes.
134	- **Cheap read-only recon** (`haiku-worker`) — locating code, mapping a surface, log analysis,
135	  run-and-report. Never writes.
136	
137	Delegate a chunk that is self-contained, heavy/noisy, or one of several independent pieces (fan
138	those out in one turn). A worker never starts or finishes the overall task and never commits
139	unless its brief says so.

  must not go cold by oversight.

    reported; a detached consultation or panel (start `c3 consult --task <task> --wait` in the
    background - its exit is the signal - or poll `--status`); a long shell job (a suite, a
    build); a window you gave another session, until it says it is done; an operator step with a
    named end ("I install it and come back"); a cooldown with a named end (a provider's
    `retry_after`, a quota window). Idle is only: none of these, and nothing can be done without
    the operator.
  - *The means in Claude Code:* a Monitor or a background wait is the primary signal; the
    `ScheduleWakeup` tool is the heartbeat - about 20 minutes (1200 s), armed at the first
    delegation or wait of the session and kept while running work goes on. Every wake: small
    reads only (a state file's tail, `c3 consult --task <task> --status`); one line when nothing
    finished. Anything finished or needing action is activity: act, and the idle count restarts.
  - *Idle:* idle wake 1 - one line in the state file ("idle since <time>"); idle wake 2 - write
    the handover on disk, stop the wakeups, and tell the operator in one line the cheap ways
    back: a fresh session from the state file; `/compact` is the operator's to run.

    while the cache is warm. In Claude Code the agent has no means to compact itself: while work
    runs, keep the context warm however long the wait; when idle, hand over as above.

  --useful yes|partly|no`). A routed panel draws its seats from these marks.

  out, or `--require` refuses the run, tell the operator who is out and until when.

While an `agy` or `muse` member runs (a single run or a panel member, detached or not), write
NOTHING under the collab directory or the working tree — `state.md`, notes and findings stores
included — and run no git command. Both engines are checked by evidence: a change during an
`agy` run FAILS that member; during a `muse` run it WARNS; either way the reviewer read a moving
target. This binds your workers too: hold a writing worker until `--status` says the run is
done, then write what you queued. (The `http` engine never touches the machine — it only warns.)

## The coordinator record

- The coordinator's session identity never reaches a reviewer child. `c3` scrubs the host
  markers (`CODEX_SESSION_ID`, the `CLAUDE_CODE_*` session ids, the messaging socket and token,
  `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, every `CODEX_SANDBOX*`, and the `ZCODE_*` / `ZCODE_PLUGIN*`)
  from every reviewer CLI and launcher probe. The ledger records the removed NAMES in
  `child_env_scrubbed`, never a value. The operator's own settings, the plugin roots and the
  provider keys are kept.
- The coordinator's identity is recorded once per run in the ledger `coordinator`
  `{provider, model, engine, host, source}`. `host` is `claude-code` when the Claude Code
  markers are present, else `unknown`. Set `CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR` to `<provider> :: <model>`
  (optionally ` [<engine>]`), a roster position `#<n>` or a provider label to name the
  coordinator's own model; a reviewer the bridge seats that IS your model gets a warning (never a
  refusal), and an unparseable value is refused before anything starts. Keep the operator's value
  when it is set — do not guess your own.

Prefer these to the host's own backgrounding. Full mechanics and exit codes: the `consult`
skill's `reference.md`.

- `c3 consult --detach ...` — run a consultation or a panel in the background, return at once
  with the detach id, its status file and the come-back commands. Checked first: a refusal comes
  back immediately, nothing written.
- `c3 consult --task <task> --status [--id <id>]` — read status only, never blocks (0 done+usable,
  1 done with a failure or died, 2 running). `--status --prune` removes files of runs done/died
  > 7 days.
- `c3 consult --task <task> --wait [--id <id>] [--wait-timeout-sec <s>]` — block until done; keep
  `<s>` below your tool's command timeout.
- `c3 consult --task <task> --kick --member <NN> [--id <id>]` — stop ONE hung member; its partial
  is salvaged and the panel goes on. Ask the operator before kicking a merely-slow member.

Park a detached run in the task's `state.md` (the detach id, the brief path, the come-back
command); a later session finds it there and in the SessionStart line.

**Quota windows (wave 8).** Before a wave of reviews on a subscription plan, read the QUOTA column of
`c3 providers` (`5h 96% until 18:32; wk 15% until Oct 20`): a quota window at 98 % or more makes
the reviewer out until its reset, like a usage limit - ask the operator whether to wait or to go on
without that reviewer. Keep review threads small: prefer `--mode new` with a brief that names the
earlier reply over forking a large thread (a parent rollout over `CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB` is refused,
it would be replayed on every tool call); the bridge stops a run at `--budget` (90 % by default) with its
partial kept, and turns the reviewer's sub-agents off.

## Supporting c3 commands

- `c3 pack --brief <b> --out <o> [--focus <glob>] [--budget <n>] [--task <t>]` — build a
  sanitizing reviewer pack (with a `.pack.json` sidecar) for the `http` engine or for a chat
  model; the index feeds the periphery when present, else a lexical neighbourhood.
- `c3 explain --claim "<c>" [--focus <glob>] [--audience <who>] --yes` — an explainer pack for
  one claim. **It leaves the machine only after you confirm** (`--yes` skips the prompt).
- `c3 snapshot [--delta] [--depth 0-9] [--budget <n>] [--focus <glob>]` — a repository snapshot,
  optionally a git delta since the last full snapshot's anchor.
- `c3 index build|rebuild|query|stats` — the local code index (embedded SurrealDB, per project; opt-in: `cargo install --features index-surreal`, else it reports `none`).
  Never required for a consultation; `query` is BM25 + reciprocal-rank with a bounded 1-hop
  expansion.
- `c3 router simulate|replay|priors|explain` — routing insight: `explain` prints the score table
  the next panel draw would use, one line per roster lineage; `replay` confirms a routed panel's
  seats from the ledger.
- `c3 telemetry status` (the on/off status and instance id), `c3 complain "<text>"` and
  `c3 forget-me` (the maintainer intake; both confirm before sending). Telemetry is on by
  default, carries outcome classes only — never task names, prompts, briefs, paths or keys — and
  `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off` switches it off.

## Worker-tier contract

Pick the tier by what the task needs; the names stay, the models behind them change.

- **Deep reasoning that needs judgment** (`opus-worker`) — novel code, multi-file debugging,
  build-and-fix loops. Writes.
- **Well-specified, pattern-following execution** (`sonnet-worker`, the default) — a known change
  across files, tests to a pattern, doc updates, running a suite and reporting. Writes.
- **Cheap read-only recon** (`haiku-worker`) — locating code, mapping a surface, log analysis,
  run-and-report. Never writes.

Delegate a chunk that is self-contained, heavy/noisy, or one of several independent pieces (fan
those out in one turn). A worker never starts or finishes the overall task and never commits
unless its brief says so.

## Worker runs (`c3 work`, design `docs/work-mode.md`)

A worker run is a roster model as an ordinary CODING WORKER for low-stakes or test work: it
reads and edits the repository, runs the test commands it is allowed, and reports. It is NOT
a consultation — no evidence check, no findings, no rating prompt, no review-ledger entry
(`c3 consult --status` never lists it). First workers (the operator's roster): GLM-5.3 and
GLM-5.3-flash (z.ai endpoint), DeepSeek-4.1-flash (byteplus endpoint) — all through the
`claude` engine, which already drives them for reviews. A roster entry opts in with
`"roles": ["worker"]` (the existing `roles` key).

```
c3 work --task <slug> --brief <file> --provider <roster label> [--model <id>]
        [--prompt <text>] [--effort low|medium|high|xhigh] [--max-turns <n>=80]
        [--timeout-sec <s>=3600] [--allow "Bash(cargo test:*)"]...
        [--detach] [--status [--id <id>]] [--wait [--id <id>]]
```

The prompt is a fixed worker preamble (never run git, never leave the repository, never
commit; finish with a final report) plus the brief file plus `--prompt`; the child runs with
the write tools (`Read,Edit,Write,Grep,Glob,Bash`, `--permission-mode acceptEdits`) under the
allow list (defaults: `Bash(cargo test|check|clippy|fmt:*)`). The record lands in
`<collab>/<task>/work/<NN>-<provider>-<model>/`: `brief.md` (the prompt as sent),
`events.jsonl` (the child's stream verbatim), `report.md` (the final assistant text),
`diff.txt` (git status before/after plus `git diff --stat`, computed by c3 — the worker
never runs git) and `run.json` (status `done|died|timeout|refused`, turns, tool calls,
files changed, usage; the argv and scrubbed env NAMES, never a secret value).

Refused before anything starts: a missing/unreadable brief, a prompt above the engine's
1 MiB cap, a label that is not a worker (the message lists the workers) or not engine
claude, the entry's `env_key` variable unset, a missing launcher, `--allow` naming git
(a worker never commits), and a second run on a task that already has a live one
(`--status` exit codes: 0 all done, 1 one died/timed out, 2 one running).

The live-member rule does NOT apply to a worker run: a worker is expected to change the
tree, so you may keep working (and writing under the collab directory) while one runs.

# C3 — claude-codex-consult in Rust

**Status: parity with claude-codex-consult 0.6.1** (the compatibility release 0.2.0; measured by
the pinned v0.6.1 harnesses through the shim - see `docs/port/harness-shim.md` and
`docs/port/rc5-verification-2026-10-09.md` when it exists; the changes in `CHANGELOG.md`).
The full surface runs. The parity port (milestones 1–6) is in the binary —
`c3 providers`, `c3 consult` (with the `codex`, `agy`, `muse`, `claude` and `http` engines),
`c3 findings` (statuses and ratings), `c3 scoreboard`, `c3 hook`, `c3 telemetry`/`complain`/
`forget-me`, the reviewer roster and the routed **panel** with detach/status/wait/prune/kick —
and so are the heavy subsystems after it: **packs and the `http` engine** (milestone 7,
run live against OpenRouter — see `docs/port/m7-status.md`), the **index** (milestone 8,
SurrealDB behind the opt-in `index-surreal` feature), the **router** (milestone 9) and the **stdio MCP server**
(milestone 10, `c3 mcp`). What is measured by which harness: milestone-1 parity by
`docs/port/m1-acceptance.md` (byte-for-byte against `codex-providers.ps1`) and the per-milestone
`m*-acceptance.md` / `m7-status.md` notes, plus `cargo test` (the c3 lib, `c3-core`, and the
`http_engine` integration suite incl. a seeded-secret grep of every written file) and
`cargo clippy -D warnings`. **Deliberately not ported: multi-host coordination.** The PowerShell
plugin coordinates from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Z Code, Kimi Code or a plain shell; C3's
coordinator host is **Claude Code only** (host-invariance across shells stays with the plugin).
The PowerShell plugin [`codex-consult`](https://github.com/xelth-com/claude-codex-consult)
remains installable (`/plugin marketplace add xelth-com/claude-codex-consult`, then
`/plugin install codex-consult@claude-codex-consult`) and its `.collab` files are byte-compatible
with C3's — either bridge reads the same task history. Its README is the specification this port
follows section by section. Page: <https://xelth.com/C3/>.

## What it is

A coordinator — your Claude Code, Codex CLI or any shell session — asks a **roster of
reviewers from different labs** to look at a one-page brief. Reviewers are read-only:
nothing is edited by them. Every consultation is recorded as files next to the code (the
brief, the reviewer's reply verbatim, a JSON ledger, **findings tracked by id** that you
verify and move yourself), and a **panel** runs several reviewers in parallel and
reconciles them. Reviewers are subscriptions the user already has: the ChatGPT plan through
the Codex CLI, z.ai GLM, Xiaomi MiMo or any Responses-API provider through a
`[model_providers.<name>]` table, Gemini through Google's Antigravity CLI `agy`, Meta Muse
through the Muse Code CLI, Claude through Claude Code headless (`claude -p`; the subscription,
an API key, or a coding plan's Anthropic-compatible endpoint). The bridge never creates, prints,
stores or commits a key. C3 adds
one API path for people who will not juggle subscriptions - OpenRouter (or any
OpenAI-compatible endpoint) through a native `http` engine that reads its key from the
environment and sends the reviewer a prepared pack instead of tools - and, on top of the
same files, packs for chat models, a local SurrealDB index and telemetry-driven panel
routing. The design is in [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md).

## Why a Rust rewrite

One static binary instead of PowerShell 5.1/7 on three OSes; a typed ledger and findings
store; the same behaviour under Claude Code, Codex CLI and a plain shell without a host
adapter (plugin ROADMAP R13, host invariance); and a place to make the bridge fast enough
to run a panel non-blocking (R12).

## Plan — port order (each step lands with tests and the plugin's evals as the oracle)

1. **Providers and preflight** — the Codex config walk (`[model_providers.*]`, `env_key`),
   `codex login status`, the roster file, the availability verdicts of `codex-providers.ps1`.
2. **One consultation** — brief → `codex exec` (and the `agy` / `muse` engines), the reply
   file with its header lines, the events stream, the `-DryRun` output byte for byte.
3. **Ledger and findings** — `sessions.json`, `findings.json`, ids, statuses, ratings,
   the atomic write order and the lock/recovery rules.
4. **Roster, panel, purposes, effort vocabularies, peak windows.**
5. **Telemetry and complaints** (plugin ROADMAP R17) — the terms below, the spool, `--complain`,
   `--forget-me`.
6. Claude Code packaging (skill, hook, evals) as a thin layer over the binary.

Steps 1-6 are the parity port. The heavy subsystems are explicit milestones after it
(see [docs/DESIGN.md](docs/DESIGN.md), section 10):

7. **Packs and the `http` engine** — snapshots and reviewer/explainer packs from one
   sanitizing builder; OpenRouter reviewers get a pack, never tools.
8. **Index** — embedded SurrealDB (per project, or one server per user across projects),
   rebuildable from files + repo, opt-in (`--features index-surreal`), never required for a consultation.
9. **Router** — panel thickness (`shadow` / `council` / `consilium`) and a versioned,
   auditable draw from the scoreboard with priors distributed by the maintainer's server.
10. **MCP server** — read-and-record tools for Claude Code without the plugin.

## The `claude` engine (plugin 0.6.0; C3 wave 4)

Claude Code headless as a reviewer, SPAWNED exactly as the plugin spawns it (no native Messages
API here - decision P4 of the parity task): `claude -p --output-format stream-json --verbose
--restricted --strict-mcp-config --disable-slash-commands --tools Read,Grep,Glob --permission-mode
dontAsk --model <m> [--effort <e>] [--json-schema <the schema TEXT>] [--max-turns <n>]
[--add-dir <dir>...] (--session-id <minted uuid> | --resume <thread> [--fork-session])`, run from
the repository root, the prompt on stdin. Replies are `handoffs/NN-claudecode-<slug>.*` (the
prefix `claude` stays the coordinator's default brief prefix: `--brief-prefix <slug>`, else
`CODEX_CONSULT_BRIEF_PREFIX`, else `claude` - the coordinator's briefs are
`handoffs/<NN>-<prefix>-<slug>.md`; a reply prefix (`codex`, `agy`, `muse`, `claudecode`, `http`)
or a value that is not a lowercase slug is refused before anything starts, and the dry run prints
`brief prefix:`). Launcher: `--engine-exe`,
`CODEX_CONSULT_CLAUDE_EXE`, `claude.exe` / `claude.cmd` / `claude` on PATH, then
`%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\claude.exe`.

- **Roster entry:** `{"provider": "anthropic", "engine": "claude", "model": "claude-opus-5-5",
  "auth": "subscription"}` (or `--engine claude --model sonnet`; the label defaults to
  `anthropic`). `model` is REQUIRED and one of the closed table: `opus`, `sonnet`, `haiku`,
  `fable`, `claude-fable-5-1`, `claude-fable-5`, `claude-opus-5-5`, `claude-opus-5`,
  `claude-opus-4-8`, `claude-opus-4-7`, `claude-opus-4-6`, `claude-sonnet-5-5`, `claude-sonnet-5`,
  `claude-sonnet-4-6`, `claude-haiku-5-5`, `claude-haiku-4-5`, each optionally ending in `[1m]`
  - spelled exactly so (the lookup is case-sensitive, as the plugin's: `OPUS` is refused).
  An alias floats: every thread is pinned to the id its first init event resolved
  (`engine_run.model_resolved`), and every later turn of it sends that id.
- **Three auth modes.** `subscription` (the default): the claude.ai login, checked by
  `claude auth status` (local, free; `ok: signed in (claude.ai subscription)`), and every turn's
  init event must name `apiKeySource none`. `api-key`: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` must be set NOW (a
  local check no ledger evidence replaces) and the init must name it. `endpoint`: a third-party
  Anthropic-compatible endpoint spelled out in the entry - `"endpoint": {"base_url":
  "https://api.z.ai/api/anthropic", "env_key": "ZAI_API_KEY", "timeout_ms": 3000000}` plus an
  optional `"plan": "zai"`; the model is the provider's own id (`glm-5.3`, never an Anthropic
  one - only a model the subscription cannot serve proves the billing), the preflight is local
  (`ok: env ZAI_API_KEY set`, no `claude auth status`, no live request; the launcher must answer
  `claude --version` - one that does not run is unavailable before any turn), and the child gets
  `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` (the value of the variable `env_key` names, read at
  the launch, never logged) and `API_TIMEOUT_MS` - and nothing else of `ANTHROPIC_*`.
- **The child environment is an ALLOW list** (system, locale, proxy and trust variables,
  `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1` set): every host marker, test-mode variable,
  inherited gateway, model override and operator variable is absent - for every turn, the sign-in
  check and the version probe alike. The ledger records the names only
  (`engine_run.child_env_allowed`).
- **Transcripts outside the tree:** a run is refused before any turn when `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`
  or the projects directory Claude Code writes its transcripts to (the one `claude auth status`
  reported, else `<CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR or ~/.claude>/projects` - every auth mode, links resolved)
  lies inside the repository under review.
- **Read-only by evidence:** every init event (a killed turn's too) must list no tool outside
  Read, Grep, Glob, StructuredOutput, no MCP server and the permission mode `dontAsk`; the model
  every assistant message names must be the pinned one; and the strict tree check fails a run
  that changed the working tree or the collab directory (managed settings and their hooks still
  apply). A turn killed on its timeout whose init failed that proof is failed with that reason
  and never continued.
- **Rate limits:** a rejecting `rate_limit_event` beside a successful result keeps the reply
  usable, warns, and records `engine_run.quota_mark` - the route (and its plan) is out until the
  reset, in this repository's ledger and in the machine-wide health file.
- **Panels:** the claude members of a panel run one at a time (one scheduling group) unless
  `"parallel": {"<label>": n}` raises their labels; a `plan` makes the plan's codex and claude
  routes one group, and a panel member waits for a run of its plan elsewhere on the machine.

The endpoint route stays where the plugin's comparison kept it: "**Decided 2026-10-08 (wave 29c,
12 pairs per plan, handoff 40 of `.collab/claude-engine-2026-09-30/`): the route STAYS for z.ai
(credits 0.27x, wall 0.46x, structured 12/12 on both routes, blind marks 4.33 vs 4.08) and for
MiMo (credits 0.17x, wall 1.16x - no faster than codex on that plan, structured 12/12 both, blind
marks 5.0 vs 3.08).**" (plugin README, "Engines (wave 29)", "Endpoint mode"). Ported in
`docs/port/wave4-claude.md`; setup text in `plugin/skills/setup-providers/SKILL.md` section 4c.

## Quota windows and the reading budget (plugin wave 30; C3 wave 8)

A subscription's quota is spent in windows - on a ChatGPT plan a 5-hour window and a weekly one -
and ONE review can spend a whole 5-hour window: a fork replays its parent's context on every tool
call, and a reviewer's own sub-agents replay theirs. C3 reads what Codex itself writes into each
thread's rollout (`<codex home>/sessions/<yyyy>/<mm>/<dd>/rollout-<ts>-<thread>.jsonl`, the last
`token_count` that names a window) and acts on it, as the plugin does (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`):

- **Ledger** (codex runs, after `commit_wait_ms`): `quota {primary, secondary, observed_at}`,
  `tokens {input, cached, output, thread_input, calls, max_input, context_window, subagents {count,
  input, calls}}` (the run's share of the thread's running total - a fork inherits its parent's),
  `subagents_allowed`, `budget`; the summary's `quota      :` line and the handoff's
  `Quota (rollout):` line.
- **Verdict**: the newest observed window of an endpoint (its ledgers, the machine-wide health
  records - which now carry `quota` - and, for the built-in `openai` endpoint while the
  machine-wide health is on, the codex home's newest rollout): at 98 % or more with its reset ahead
  the endpoint is `unavailable (5-hour window 99 % used, resets <iso>)` like a usage limit with a
  known reset (roster walk, `--require`, panel, `--short`, a real run refused); at 80 % or more the
  verdict says `available (low quota: 5-hour window 84 % until 18:32)`. `c3 providers` has a QUOTA
  column (`5h 96% until 18:32; wk 15% until Oct 20`) and `--json` rows a `quota` object.
- **Plan caps (`ext.c3.plan_caps`, `ext.c3.reset_hint`)**: a roster entry whose plan has a monthly /
  weekly / daily cap may say so under its own `ext` (`"ext": {"c3": {"plan_caps": ["monthly"],
  "reset_hint": "monthly:27T00:00+08:00"}}`; the plugin ignores `ext`). Two instant 429s with no
  window text within an hour (distinct consultations, newer than the last usable reply) then mark the
  entry `unavailable (plan quota: 429 twice in <n> min, no window text; retry after <iso>)` until the
  hint's next reset instead of the 10-minute burst. That is INFERRED exhaustion, not evidence: the
  hint is the operator's statement about the plan; without one the entry is out until the pair is 24 h old and then
  probed (eligible again - not proof that capacity returned; another instant 429 marks it out
  again); a transient pair on a capped plan costs the time to the reset - clear it with a
  successful explicit run (`--skip-preflight`: the verdict is advisory for a direct run) or by
  editing the hint.
- **`--budget <percent>`** (env `CODEX_CONSULT_QUOTA_BUDGET`, default 90, 0 = off): the stall watch
  reads the run's rollout every 15 s and stops the main turn at the budget - the partial kept, no
  continuation, `failed: stopped at the quota budget: 5-hour window 91 % used, resets 18:32; the
  partial is kept` (provider_failure class `operator`, telemetry class `quota`).
- **Replay guard**: a `--mode fork|resume` whose parent rollout is over `CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB`
  (default 512) is refused before anything starts; from 128 KB on it is warned about.
- **Sub-agents off**: every codex turn passes `-c features.multi_agent=false` right after `-m`
  unless `--codex-config` (or the roster's `codex_config`) names `features.multi_agent`.
- **Reading discipline**: the purpose paragraphs of acceptance, diff-review, checkpoint and
  core-contract end with the plugin's block (`git diff <range> --stat` first, one path at a time
  with a line cap, the documents first, the verdict even on an incomplete read).

## Telemetry (on by default, off with one line)

Installing C3 means accepting these terms. C3 reports **one anonymous event per
consultation** (and one per usefulness rating) to the maintainer's intake,
<https://xelth.com/T/>, so the bridge can be improved when someone the maintainer never hears
from uses it. Everything collected is shown in the open, as counts, on <https://xelth.com/C3/>.

* **Sent - classes only:** `app_id` (`c3`), the C3 version, an instance id
  (`sha256(salt file + machine name)` — stable per installation, meaningless elsewhere), a
  severity, and `details`: the engine, the reviewer's VENDOR CLASS and model (below), the purpose
  (one of the eight purposes, `none` or `other`), the outcome class (`usable`,
  `usable-after-continuation`, `failed:<class>` with a closed class), wall seconds, token counts,
  findings counts, structured or not, a format retry or not, panel size, the federation peer
  COUNT, OS, runtime, and `consult_ref` (below). `tags` repeat `[provider, model]`.
* **The rating event** (`c3 findings --rate`, `c3 telemetry --backfill-ratings`): `details` exactly
  `engine, provider, model, purpose, mark, age_days, bridge_version, os, ps_version, judge,
  rating_rev, consult_ref` (the plugin's 0.6.1 shape; `ps_version` is `unknown` - C3 runs no
  PowerShell), `title` the mark, `client_time` the MARK's own time on every path. `judge` is
  `{provider, model, source}` - who gave the mark, resolved at rating time and saved in the mark:
  `rating_actor` (`CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR` of the rating process), `consult_coordinator` (the
  coordinator the consultation recorded) or `unknown` - classes only, never a label or a host.
  `rating_rev` is the mark's revision (1 + the consultation's highest); the intake keeps per
  `(instance_id, consult_ref)` the rating with the highest `rating_rev`.
* **`consult_ref`:** a random id minted for each consultation (a lower-case guid, derived from
  nothing - not the `consult_id` the reviewer sees), kept in the ledger right after `consult_id`
  and sent in the consultation event and every rating event of it, so the intake can link them.
  A pseudonymous correlation key: whoever holds both the telemetry and a shared `sessions.json`
  can join them on it.
* **The classes** (the plugin's closed vendor table; `c3/src/telemetry/classes.rs`): the vendor
  class is derived from the HOST of the endpoint the reviewer talked to (`openai` - also Codex's
  built-in provider -, `zai`, `xiaomi`, `byteplus`, `moonshot`, `alibaba`, `minimax`), else from
  the engine (`agy` google, `muse` meta, `claude` anthropic), else `other`; the model is sent only
  when it EQUALS an entry of that class's closed list (after lower-casing, `[1m]` stripped),
  else `other` (`unknown` without a model). A roster label, a model or a purpose as typed - say
  `customer-acme` - never leaves the machine. **C3 extension (the `http` engine):** the host
  `openrouter.ai` is the class `openrouter`; its model is sent in OpenRouter's `<vendor>/<model>`
  form only when the vendor slug is one of `openai`, `anthropic`, `google`, `z-ai`, `moonshotai`,
  `minimax`, `xiaomi`, `qwen` (alibaba's list), `meta-llama` (meta's list) AND the model part
  equals an entry of that class's list (`openai/gpt-5.1`), else `other`; an http endpoint of a
  listed vendor's host takes that vendor's class, any other host `other`.
* **Never:** task names, prompts, briefs, paths, thread ids, `consult_id`, finding texts, notes,
  topics, labels as typed, the coordinator's host, user names, keys. The server drops
  secret-named keys on arrival and reports how many; C3 treats a non-zero count as its own bug.
* **Off:** `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off` (any value other than unset/`on`/`1`/`true`/`yes`
  counts as off), or `--telemetry off` per run - a run's own `--telemetry on|off` wins over the
  variable, and a panel passes it to its members. The first run after an install prints this
  notice once; the dry run says whether it is on.
* **Never blocks a run; never lost silently:** events queue in C3's own outbox
  (`<codex home>/c3/telemetry/spool.ndjson`, one `{v, kind, queued_unix, body}` line each - not
  the plugin's `telemetry-spool/`: C3 is its own app with its own salt and instance id), are sent
  by a detached sender a run starts right after its commit (a consultation, a panel - once -, a
  rating, a backfill; the run never waits for it, and it gets an allow-listed environment only: no
  key, no host marker) in batches of at most 100 (one flush ends after 60 s, one request after 8 s),
  retried by the next sender and dropped 7 days after they were queued. The sender follows the
  intake's answers as the plugin does: a 429 whose `Retry-After` is at most 60 s is waited for
  once (else the batch stays queued), a 400 naming `events[i]` drops that event and resends the
  rest (at most three per flush), a 413 halves the batch and drops an event too large alone -
  each refused event is one line of the last flush's `rejected` - and a 403, another refusal or no
  answer stops the flush with the outbox kept. Appends and the sender are synchronised by a lock,
  and the sender removes only the lines it delivered or dropped - an event queued while it sends
  stays queued. The sender lock's owner record (`flush.owner.json`) lets `--status` and a refused
  sender say "sender busy since <t>", and after 30 minutes "sender stuck since <t> (pid <n>)". An event that cannot be
  spooled is said and counted (`c3 telemetry --status`); a rating's event is retried and else
  left for `c3 telemetry --backfill-ratings`.
* **Complaints:** `c3 --complain "<text>"` prints the exact payload (your text plus the last
  ledger entry's summary - classes only), asks before sending, and prints a public reference
  like `T-7KQ4-M2XZ` to quote on the forum section <https://xelth.com/F/p/c3> or in a mail.
* **Delete my data:** `c3 forget-me` (or `c3 telemetry --forget --public-ref <ref> [--local]`,
  or `DELETE https://xelth.com/T/v2/instances/<instance_id>?public_ref=<ref>`) asks the intake to
  remove every event and complaint this installation ever sent - proved by a complaint's public
  reference - and removes the local salt, outbox and references only AFTER the intake confirmed
  it. A DELETE the intake does not confirm deletes nothing locally: the instance id and the
  reference stay, the pending deletion is recorded (`forget-pending.json`) and nothing is
  spooled or sent until `c3 forget-me` retries it with the same identity and the intake
  confirms. Without any public reference the intake cannot verify ownership:
  `c3 forget-me --local` (or `c3 telemetry --forget --local`) removes the local data only, and
  says that the intake keeps what was sent.
* **`c3 telemetry`:** `--status` (the switch and its source, the intake, the outbox, the events
  not spooled since the last flush, the sender lock's owner, a pending deletion, the last flush,
  the instance id),
  `--flush`, `--forget`, `--backfill-ratings [--dry-run]`. The intake is
  `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY_URL` when set (https only; plain http only to a loopback host in test
  mode), else `https://xelth.com/T`.

## Build

```sh
cargo build --release          # target/release/c3
./target/release/c3 --version
./target/release/c3 providers --short   # the reviewer availability line
cargo test && cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings
```

### Light bundle or indexed bundle

- **Light bundle (the default).** `cargo install --path crates/c3-cli` builds without
  SurrealDB, in minutes; `c3 index` reports `none`. Every consultation works: the reviewers
  that run through Codex, Claude Code, agy and muse read the repository themselves.
- **Indexed bundle.** `cargo install --path crates/c3-cli --features index-surreal` adds the
  embedded SurrealDB code index (~26 min more to build, ~180 MiB store per project). Build it
  for the `http` engine's reviewer packs and the planned browser engine, where the pack's
  periphery comes from the index.
- **Invariant:** the index is never required for a consultation. (Flipped 2026-10-14: the
  index is opt-in.) CI builds the default on Linux and Windows and the indexed bundle on Linux.

### Platforms

Windows 11 is where every harness ran and where the PowerShell plugin's evals are the oracle;
since the Linux port (`docs/port/linux-port.md`) the same tree builds, lints and tests on
Ubuntu x86_64 too, and `.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs fmt, clippy and the test suites on
`ubuntu-latest` and `windows-latest` (the `index-surreal` build only on Ubuntu). What differs on
Linux: process liveness and the tree kill come from `/proc` and `kill` instead of the Win32
APIs and `taskkill /T`, the file locks are `flock` advisory locks instead of share modes, and
a detached run is a child in its own process group instead of a `cmd.exe` launch; the files
written are the same bytes. The tests that need Windows (cmd.exe launchers, Windows launcher
paths) are gated `#[cfg(windows)]` with a reason each. macOS is untested. For a sandbox whose
egress proxy carries the credential and re-terminates TLS, the `http` engine honours
`HTTPS_PROXY`, `C3_HTTP_AUTH_PROXY=<host,...>` (no `Authorization` header, no key read) and
`C3_HTTP_CA_BUNDLE=<pem>` (extra trust anchors) — see `docs/port/linux-port.md`.

A cargo workspace of three crates: `crates/c3-core` (contracts and file formats),
`crates/c3` (runtime modules), `crates/c3-cli` (the binary). Each ported piece brings its
own dependencies when it needs them; SurrealDB arrives with milestone 8 behind the opt-in `index-surreal` feature.
The plugin's harnesses can drive the binary through `tests/shim/` (see
`docs/port/harness-shim.md`); `docs/port/m1-acceptance.md` lists the assertions milestone 1
answers to.

### Known limits (0.2.0)

- **Shared health journal with plugin 0.6.1:** with plugin 0.6.1 on the same machine the
  once-only replay of a kept journal record holds only for C3's own updates; the plugin's updater
  can re-apply a record the cap evicted until plugin 0.6.2 (its T14) - `docs/port/wave2b-compat.md`,
  "Limits".
- **Claude endpoint preflight:** the `claude --version` probe proves the launcher runs, not that it
  takes a `-p` turn; a launcher that answers `--version` but rejects the turn fails its first turn,
  and one whose `--version` needs the token is reported unavailable - `docs/port/wave4-claude.md`.
- **Claude transcript guard:** the derived location reads the child's `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, else
  `USERPROFILE` (Windows) or `HOME` (elsewhere) - Claude Code's `os.homedir()` sources - and
  refuses when neither is set; a wrapper launcher that sets `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` inside itself is
  not seen before the spawn (the strict tree check fails such a run after its turn).
- **No kill without a record:** a reviewer tree is killed only when the record naming it is on
  disk - the recovery record, its fallback or `<codex home>/c3/pending-kill/<task>-<run id>.json`;
  all three failing, the tree is left alive and the task refused while it runs. A helper left by an
  EXTERNAL death of its recorded ancestors (not by C3), below an unrecorded intermediate and with a
  command line unrelated to codex, is not detectable by either bridge -
  `docs/port/wave7-acceptance-fixes.md`, "7b".

## Install into Claude Code

`plugin/` is a Claude Code plugin directory: a `SessionStart` hook and three skills
(`consult`, `coordinate`, `setup-providers`) with brief and role templates and an `evals/`
suite — a thin layer over the `c3` binary built above, carrying no reviewer logic of its own.
Install the binary first (`cargo install --path crates/c3-cli`, or a release download, on
`PATH` or pointed at with `C3_EXE=<path>`), then add the plugin directory in Claude Code
(`/plugin marketplace add`, then `/plugin install`, against this repository or a local
checkout). The plugin does **not** ship the `c3 mcp` server enabled — a skills-driven Claude
Code session already has the surface, and an always-on server would be a second, unguided way
in; add it opt-in with a repo-root `.mcp.json` (see `docs/port/mcp.md`). See
[plugin/README.md](plugin/README.md) for the exact commands, prerequisites and how it relates
to the PowerShell [`codex-consult`](https://github.com/xelth-com/claude-codex-consult) plugin
(both can be installed side by side; their `.collab` files are byte-compatible). The
switch-over procedure from the PowerShell plugin to C3 is
[docs/port/phase2-switch.md](docs/port/phase2-switch.md).

Another Claude Code session on the same machine, from a local checkout: `claude plugin marketplace
add <path to the C3 checkout>`, then `claude plugin install c3@c3` (the marketplace is named `c3`;
user scope; other sessions pick it up at their next restart), and the binary
`cargo install --path crates/c3-cli --force` (the light bundle; add
`--features index-surreal` for the embedded SurrealDB index - see "Light bundle or indexed bundle"). Once a newer plugin version is published (the version is
bumped at each release), `claude plugin update c3@c3`.

# Changelog

All notable changes to C3 are recorded here. The format follows
[Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.1.0/); the versions follow
[Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/). The specification of every compatibility wave is the
PowerShell plugin [`claude-codex-consult`](https://github.com/xelth-com/claude-codex-consult) at its
tag `v0.6.1`; the finding ids (Fnn-k, En, Dn) are those of the parity task's reviews and of the
plugin's own waves. Each wave's details are in `docs/port/wave*.md`.

## [Unreleased]

## [0.2.2] - 2026-10-15

- Build: the `index-surreal` feature (embedded SurrealDB code index) is now opt-in - the default `cargo install` is the light bundle; `--features index-surreal` for the http/browser packs (README 'Light bundle or indexed bundle').

### Fixed

- **Wave 9 - the four consilium defects (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`)**: (D1) a panel starts new threads for every member unless `--mode fork` is given, and the header prints the mode; (D2) C3's own lines name `c3 consult --task <t> --status --id <id>` / `--wait --id <id>` / `c3 providers` / `c3 findings`, not the plugin's `.ps1` scripts (the shims keep the plugin spelling for the harness oracle via `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT=1`); (D3) a detached single run holds the task lock only for its bookkeeping, so detached runs of one task run side by side; (D4) a roster entry may declare `ext.c3.plan_caps` / `reset_hint`, and two instant 429s inside an hour mark it out until the cap's reset instead of the 10-minute burst.
- **Wave 9b - the review of wave 9**: a detached run is admitted only beside records of a live owning bridge (never survivors, unverified processes or a dead bridge); the reservation is durable and verified before the task lock is released; the cap pair counts distinct consultations (the machine record carries `consult_id`); a non-ASCII `reset_hint` is a validation error, not a panic; the shims set `C3_PLUGIN_COMPAT` for their child only; the cap policy is documented as inferred exhaustion (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9c - the round-2 review**: the cap pair is counted by consultation identity only (same non-empty consult id = one hit; different ids are distinct at any instant; a legacy row matches a ledger row only when endpoint, failure text and the second all agree), and the admission test no longer needs PowerShell (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9d - the acceptance review**: the cap pair is built from id-carrying rows only (a row without a consult id keeps the plain 10-minute burst) and only from hits younger than 24 h at READ time, so neither a legacy mirror nor an unpruned old row can produce or prolong the cap verdict (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9e - the second acceptance pass (F76-1)**: the read-time bound on a cap-pair hit is now the entry's current cap period, not a flat 24 h, so a hinted entry stays out until its declared reset (a hit counts while `next_cap_reset(hint, hit) > now`) while an unhinted entry keeps the 24 h bound; `endpoint_health` retains id-carrying hits for 35 days and `plan_cap_verdict` applies the per-entry rule, keeping the verdict identical across every reader (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9f - the third acceptance pass (F78-1, F78-2)**: the cap detector takes the newest qualifying pair of in-period hits (a later isolated 429 no longer hides an established pair), and machine-health retention keeps id-carrying instant-429 cap evidence for 35 days regardless of its expired burst `until` with the 500-record cap evicting such evidence last, so a reader in another repository still sees the pair until the declared reset (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9g - the fourth acceptance pass (F80-1)**: `update_machine_health` now durably drops cap evidence superseded by a newer clearing success (a usable reply) before retention and the record cap run, so the asymmetric lifetimes of evidence (35 days, evicted last) and the success (24 h, evicted first) can no longer resurrect an obsolete refusal for a machine-only reader (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9h - the fifth acceptance pass (F82-1)**: the newest clearing success of an endpoint is now a durable anchor - kept 35 days and evicted only in the record cap's last tier, after cap evidence - so a success can no longer be discarded while its cap pair waits in a busy (exclusively held) journal; evidence arriving late from a skipped journal or a delayed retry is still superseded (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).
- **Wave 9i - the sixth acceptance pass (F84-1)**: exactly one clearing anchor per endpoint (the newest success, ties broken by record key) is protected, so redundant equal-time successes are ordinary rows and can no longer fill the cap's protected tier and evict another endpoint's only clearing proof (`docs/port/wave9-consilium-defects.md`).


## [0.2.1] - 2026-10-14

- Plugin: the coordinate skill carries the waiting rule (wakeups instead of blocking waits); the SessionStart hook prints it; README: the local-checkout install path.

### Fixed

- **Wave 8j - one total order per window (8i caveat)**: every quota instant comparison is made at whole-second granularity and a tie goes to the rank, with the legacy windows resolved from a separate slot, so the pick is the same for every candidate order (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
- **Wave 8i - lossless quota instants (F62-1)**: the per-window instants keep their fractional seconds, a comparison involving a whole-second instant is made at second granularity (a tie goes to the rank), and a legacy record's unknown window instants never win on recency against a known one (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
- **Wave 8h - per-window instants persisted (F60-1)**: the quota record (ledger entry, machine-wide health record) carries `primary_observed_at` / `secondary_observed_at` for each present window, read by the recorded selection; the aggregate `observed_at` is only the fallback for older records (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).
- **Wave 8g - per-window observation instants (F58-1)**: each retained quota window keeps its own observation instant through the rollout, account and recorded/live aggregation, so a partial newer observation can no longer promote an older window (`docs/port/wave8-quota.md`).

# Coordinate (c3)

The C3 port supports one coordinator host: **Claude Code**. This skill is the coordination
layer over the `c3` binary. (The multi-host coordination story — Codex CLI, Z Code, Kimi Code,
a plain shell — stays with the `codex-consult` PowerShell bridge and is deliberately not ported
here.) The consultation procedure itself is the `consult` skill; wiring reviewers is
`setup-providers`.

## Invariants

- **You are the coordinator and the judge by default.** Workers execute, reviewers advise, you
  decide and verify. Never redo a worker's work once it reports — read the report and verify in
  your own loop; what still needs checking is a new, scoped task.
- **One objective per worker.** Brief it precisely the first time: the objective, the exact
  files, the numbers its result is measured against, what it must not touch, the report shape. A
  launch, a wait and a re-brief cost more than a brief written once.
- **English to reviewers and workers.** Briefs, prompts and handoff titles are in English;
  source material in another language is translated or summarised, never pasted.
- **Wait without blocking; keep the prompt cache warm.** Poll a state file or `c3 consult --task
  <task> --status`; never sit in a blocking foreground wait longer than the shell tool's limit.
  After the cache's lifetime the next request re-writes the whole context, so a large context
  must not go cold by oversight.
  - *Running work* (keeps the wake armed, idle count zero): a worker or subagent that has not
    reported; a detached consultation or panel (start `c3 consult --task <task> --wait` in the
    background - its exit is the signal - or poll `--status`); a long shell job (a suite, a
    build); a window you gave another session, until it says it is done; an operator step with a
    named end ("I install it and come back"); a cooldown with a named end (a provider's
    `retry_after`, a quota window). Idle is only: none of these, and nothing can be done without
    the operator.
  - *The means in Claude Code:* a Monitor or a background wait is the primary signal; the
    `ScheduleWakeup` tool is the heartbeat - about 20 minutes (1200 s), armed at the first
    delegation or wait of the session and kept while running work goes on. Every wake: small
    reads only (a state file's tail, `c3 consult --task <task> --status`); one line when nothing
    finished. Anything finished or needing action is activity: act, and the idle count restarts.
  - *Idle:* idle wake 1 - one line in the state file ("idle since <time>"); idle wake 2 - write
    the handover on disk, stop the wakeups, and tell the operator in one line the cheap ways
    back: a fresh session from the state file; `/compact` is the operator's to run.
  - *Compaction* only at a wave boundary (the report is read, the state is on disk) and only
    while the cache is warm. In Claude Code the agent has no means to compact itself: while work
    runs, keep the context warm however long the wait; when idle, hand over as above.
- **Rate every consultation** once its reply is read (`c3 findings --task <task> --rate <n>
  --useful yes|partly|no`). A routed panel draws its seats from these marks.
- **Ask the operator before going on without a required reviewer** — when one the topic needs is
  out, or `--require` refuses the run, tell the operator who is out and until when.

## The live-member rule

While an `agy` or `muse` member runs (a single run or a panel member, detached or not), write
NOTHING under the collab directory or the working tree — `state.md`, notes and findings stores
included — and run no git command. Both engines are checked by evidence: a change during an
`agy` run FAILS that member; during a `muse` run it WARNS; either way the reviewer read a moving
target. This binds your workers too: hold a writing worker until `--status` says the run is
done, then write what you queued. (The `http` engine never touches the machine — it only warns.)

## The coordinator record

- The coordinator's session identity never reaches a reviewer child. `c3` scrubs the host
  markers (`CODEX_SESSION_ID`, the `CLAUDE_CODE_*` session ids, the messaging socket and token,
  `CLAUDE_PID`, `CLAUDE_EFFORT`, every `CODEX_SANDBOX*`, and the `ZCODE_*` / `ZCODE_PLUGIN*`)
  from every reviewer CLI and launcher probe. The ledger records the removed NAMES in
  `child_env_scrubbed`, never a value. The operator's own settings, the plugin roots and the
  provider keys are kept.
- The coordinator's identity is recorded once per run in the ledger `coordinator`
  `{provider, model, engine, host, source}`. `host` is `claude-code` when the Claude Code
  markers are present, else `unknown`. Set `CODEX_CONSULT_COORDINATOR` to `<provider> :: <model>`
  (optionally ` [<engine>]`), a roster position `#<n>` or a provider label to name the
  coordinator's own model; a reviewer the bridge seats that IS your model gets a warning (never a
  refusal), and an unparseable value is refused before anything starts. Keep the operator's value
  when it is set — do not guess your own.

## The bridge's own background means

Prefer these to the host's own backgrounding. Full mechanics and exit codes: the `consult`
skill's `reference.md`.

- `c3 consult --detach ...` — run a consultation or a panel in the background, return at once
  with the detach id, its status file and the come-back commands. Checked first: a refusal comes
  back immediately, nothing written.
- `c3 consult --task <task> --status [--id <id>]` — read status only, never blocks (0 done+usable,
  1 done with a failure or died, 2 running). `--status --prune` removes files of runs done/died
  > 7 days.
- `c3 consult --task <task> --wait [--id <id>] [--wait-timeout-sec <s>]` — block until done; keep
  `<s>` below your tool's command timeout.
- `c3 consult --task <task> --kick --member <NN> [--id <id>]` — stop ONE hung member; its partial
  is salvaged and the panel goes on. Ask the operator before kicking a merely-slow member.

**Quota windows (wave 8).** Before a wave of reviews on a subscription plan, read the QUOTA column of
`c3 providers` (`5h 96% until 18:32; wk 15% until Oct 20`): a quota window at 98 % or more makes
the reviewer out until its reset, like a usage limit - ask the operator whether to wait or to go on
without that reviewer. Keep review threads small: prefer `--mode new` with a brief that names the
earlier reply over forking a large thread (a parent rollout over `CODEX_CONSULT_FORK_MAX_KB` is refused,
it would be replayed on every tool call); the bridge stops a run at `--budget` (90 % by default) with its
partial kept, and turns the reviewer's sub-agents off.

## Supporting c3 commands

- `c3 pack --brief <b> --out <o> [--focus <glob>] [--budget <n>] [--task <t>]` — build a
  sanitizing reviewer pack (with a `.pack.json` sidecar) for the `http` engine or for a chat
  model; the index feeds the periphery when present, else a lexical neighbourhood.
- `c3 explain --claim "<c>" [--focus <glob>] [--audience <who>] --yes` — an explainer pack for
  one claim. **It leaves the machine only after you confirm** (`--yes` skips the prompt).
- `c3 snapshot [--delta] [--depth 0-9] [--budget <n>] [--focus <glob>]` — a repository snapshot,
  optionally a git delta since the last full snapshot's anchor.
- `c3 index build|rebuild|query|stats` — the local code index (embedded SurrealDB, per project; opt-in: `cargo install --features index-surreal`, else it reports `none`).
  Never required for a consultation; `query` is BM25 + reciprocal-rank with a bounded 1-hop
  expansion.
- `c3 router simulate|replay|priors|explain` — routing insight: `explain` prints the score table
  the next panel draw would use, one line per roster lineage; `replay` confirms a routed panel's
  seats from the ledger.
- `c3 telemetry status` (the on/off status and instance id), `c3 complain "<text>"` and
  `c3 forget-me` (the maintainer intake; both confirm before sending). Telemetry is on by
  default, carries outcome classes only — never task names, prompts, briefs, paths or keys — and
  `CODEX_CONSULT_TELEMETRY=off` switches it off.

## Worker-tier contract

Pick the tier by what the task needs; the names stay, the models behind them change.

- **Deep reasoning that needs judgment** (`opus-worker`) — novel code, multi-file debugging,
  build-and-fix loops. Writes.
- **Well-specified, pattern-following execution** (`sonnet-worker`, the default) — a known change
  across files, tests to a pattern, doc updates, running a suite and reporting. Writes.
- **Cheap read-only recon** (`haiku-worker`) — locating code, mapping a surface, log analysis,
  run-and-report. Never writes.

Delegate a chunk that is self-contained, heavy/noisy, or one of several independent pieces (fan
those out in one turn). A worker never starts or finishes the overall task and never commits
unless its brief says so.
